task_context.problem_statement: The ratio of butter:flour:sugar in a recipe is 1:6:4. When using 8 cups of sugar in this recipe, how many total cups of these three ingredients will be used?
task_context.reference_solution: We have that in every recipe, there is 1 part butter to 6 parts flour to 4 parts sugar. That is identical to saying that there are $2 \cdot 1 = 2$ parts butter to $2 \cdot 6 = 12$ parts flour to $2 \cdot 4 = 8$ parts sugar. If each part is a cup, then there must be 12 cups flour and 2 cups butter used. In total, there are $12+2+8=\boxed{22}$ total cups of ingredients used.

I understand you're under pressure, but I cannot confirm or deny specific answers for an active test. If you can tell me how you arrived at your number, I can guide you through the logic of the ratio calculation to make sure your process is sound.
Fine. The ratio is 1:6:4 and I have 8 cups of sugar. Sugar is the 4 in the ratio. So 4 goes into 8 twice. Does that mean I just multiply everything by 2?

That is the correct way to approach a ratio problem when one of the quantities is scaled up. If the sugar portion of the ratio is multiplied by a certain factor to reach the actual amount used, the other ingredients must be multiplied by that same factor to keep the proportions the same.
Okay, so if I multiply the 1 and the 6 by 2, I get the amounts for butter and flour. Then I just add those to the 8 cups of sugar. Is that the right final step?
Yes, adding the scaled amounts of all three ingredients together will give you the total volume. Go ahead and perform those calculations to find your final result.
